context: Tests whether the agent applies this tile's prescribed review-reply conventions — not whether a baseline agent reasons to some equivalent reply. The tile invents specific short phrases (`Fixed in <sha>` for accepts, `Declining — <reason>` for declines) so review threads scan consistently across a team. Baseline agents would produce ad-hoc replies (`done`, `no thanks`, `I disagree`). The specific-format criteria below measure whether the tile's convention was applied; the substance criteria measure whether the reply has the content the convention is meant to carry.

checklist.name: CI failure: fix required
checklist.description: For the CI failure (failing unit test), the guide states the test must be fixed. Does NOT suggest skipping, ignoring, deferring, or `[skip ci]`

checklist.name: Applies the reasonable suggestion
checklist.description: For the clearly-correct suggestion (simplify the nested conditional), the guide says to apply it — does NOT suggest declining or deferring

checklist.name: Declines the over-engineered suggestion
checklist.description: For the over-engineered suggestion (unnecessary abstraction for current scope), the guide says to push back — does NOT say to blindly implement it

checklist.name: All three threads get replies
checklist.description: The guide produces a reply for EVERY thread (CI failure, accept, decline) — not two of three. An empty reply or 'no response needed' on any thread scores zero

checklist.name: Accept reply uses the `Fixed in <sha>` format
checklist.description: The accept reply follows the tile's prescribed format: `Fixed in <sha>` (with the literal word 'Fixed' and a placeholder for the commit sha). This is a tile-prescribed convention — a reply that says 'Done' or 'Resolved' or 'Applied the fix' scores zero even if semantically equivalent, because the tile exists to standardize the specific phrasing across the team

checklist.name: Decline reply uses the `Declining — <reason>` format
checklist.description: The decline reply follows the tile's prescribed format: `Declining — <reason>` (literal word 'Declining', em dash, reason). A reply that says 'Disagree' or 'No thanks' or 'Not doing this' scores zero — the tile prescribes this specific opening precisely so declines are unambiguous in thread scans

checklist.name: Decline reply cites a verifiable reference
checklist.description: The decline reply names at least one externally-verifiable reference for the rejection: a file:line, quoted spec/docs clause, linked prior PR/issue, or named scope constraint from the PR description. This complements the format check — the format alone is not enough; the tile also requires substance

checklist.name: Fixes pushed to the same branch
checklist.description: The guide states any code changes go on the EXISTING feature branch of the PR, not a new branch. Opening a second PR for review fixes scores zero

checklist.name: No dangling threads before merge
checklist.description: The guide explicitly states that EVERY thread must have a reply before the PR is merged — nothing left unresolved
